overview.text: The Chinese (Taiwan) Cobra is one of the commonest venomous snakes in southern China and causes many snakebites there.

identification.text: A hood mark that can look like spectacles, a mask, a horseshoe or an O, and a clearly pale throat.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually 1.2 to 1.5 m, rarely up to 2 m.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: South-eastern China south of the Yangtze (including Hong Kong and Hainan), Taiwan, northern Laos and northern Vietnam.

behaviour.text: Active by day and at dusk. It usually escapes from people but can be very defensive if cornered.

reproduction.text: Lays 6 to 23 eggs between May and July.

recognise.text: Spreads a hood with a variable pale mark.
